resources.string: An e-ink look for your OLED screen
On — the screen refreshes like paper
Paused for a few minutes — turns back on by itself
Turn on the PaperScreen accessibility service to use PaperScreen.
The minimum time between refreshes. Standard is the fastest Android allows: about three captures of each window per second.
Steps the greys into a few distinct levels, like e-ink. Off keeps smooth, continuous greyscale.
Partial refreshes leave a brief afterimage of what changed. Off swaps changed areas cleanly.
Every so often the whole screen flashes inverted to clear leftovers, like an e-ink page turn. Off makes every refresh partial.
Refresh only when the screen changes
Only captures the screen when apps report a change. Turn off to capture on every interval, which also catches video and games.
Applies the current filter to this screen while held.

PaperScreen draws its filtered screen as an accessibility overlay. That\'s the only kind of overlay Android lets be fully opaque while your taps still reach the apps underneath. The same service captures each window underneath the overlay, so the overlay never has to get out of the way. Captures stay on your phone.\n\nOn the next screen, open Installed apps (or Downloaded apps), choose PaperScreen, and turn it on. Then come back here.
\n\nIf the switch is greyed out as a \"restricted setting\", open App info for PaperScreen, tap ⋮ in the top corner, choose \"Allow restricted settings\", and try again.
Couldn\'t start PaperScreen. Make sure its accessibility service is on, then try again.

A page-style home screen: clock, date, favourites and an alphabetical list of apps, all as text. Long-press a favourite on the home screen to change it. Turning this off opens the system\'s default home app setting.
Alphabet index. Tap a letter to jump to it.
Secure app — tap pause to view
Shown while PaperScreen is filtering your screen, with buttons to pause or stop it.
Shows your screen in e-ink style

PaperScreen redraws your screen in the style of an e-ink display, redrawing only what changes and occasionally clearing the screen with a full refresh. It uses this service to draw a full-screen overlay that your taps pass through, and to take a screenshot of each window underneath it, which it filters and shows on the overlay. It reads the window list only to know what to capture, and doesn\'t read or change anything inside apps. Captures stay on your phone.
